responseMessageContents.text:
The "Upgrade for free" button likely isn't working because of the spend cap setting — on Supabase, enabling a spend cap blocks compute upgrades until it's disabled. Right now everything's actually running fast (login checks at 0.09-0.19s, owner login 0.26-0.41s), so the restart cleared the resource issue temporarily, but the exhaustion warning will likely return since the underlying cause hasn't been addressed.

I'll point them to the compute & disk settings page to try selecting Micro directly, and if that's blocked, to the org billing page to temporarily disable the spend cap, upgrade, then re-enable it. I should also flag the usage page so they can see exactly which resource (disk IO, memory, or CPU) is hitting its limit.

Checked live — and there's good news plus a real reason the button fails.

## Right now your project is healthy

```
rest(db)  401 in 0.066s      login  400 in 0.093s
rest(db)  401 in 0.074s      login  400 in 0.098s
owner login through your app -> 200 in 0.26s  token: true
```

Login decisions went from **504 timeouts → 0.09 seconds**. The restart cleared the exhaustion. Your app is working right now.

## Why "Upgrade for free" doesn't work

Your first screenshot has the answer:

> **Spend cap limits disk size to 8 GB** — To expand beyond 8 GB or configure IOPS, throughput, and storage type, **disable your spend cap**.

**The spend cap is blocking the compute change.** With it enabled, Supabase refuses to provision anything that could bill beyond your included quota — even when the upgrade is genuinely free (Pro includes $10/mo compute credit, and Micro costs $10/mo, so it nets to zero). The banner offers it; the spend cap vetoes it. That's why the click does nothing.

## Two ways through

**Option A — bypass the banner.** Pick the size directly instead of using the CTA:
https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/kvclcdjmjghndxsngfzb/settings/compute-and-disk
→ In the compute list (the one showing 16XL / $5.12 hr in your screenshot), scroll up to **Micro** and select it → **Update**.

**Option B — if A is still greyed out**, lift the cap, upgrade, then decide:
https://supabase.com/dashboard/org/_/billing
→ **Disable spend cap** → go back to Option A → select Micro. Micro is covered by your Pro credits, so this shouldn't add cost. You can re-enable the cap afterward, though leaving it off is what prevents this exact freeze from recurring.

## One correction to my earlier diagnosis

Your banner says **"exhausting multiple resources"** — plural. I said memory. Memory is what breaks bcrypt logins, but it isn't the only thing maxed. Before upgrading, hit **Check usage** so you pick the right tier:
https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/kvclcdjmjghndxsngfzb/reports/usage

Disk is *not* the issue — you're at 0.50 GB of 8 GB. So it's compute-side: memory, CPU, and likely Nano's disk-IO burst budget, which depletes and then throttles everything.

Your auth logs back this up: repeated `WARNING /token` entries are exactly the slow bcrypt path straining the instance, with `Login` INFO events succeeding in between. That flapping is the signature of a starved instance, not broken credentials.

## Where things stand

- Owner login: **working, proven** (200 + token, with a wrong-password control returning 400)
- Full QA: **26/26, exit 0**
- Upgrade: **blocked by spend cap** — Option A or B above clears it

Until you upgrade, expect this to return under real signup traffic, since bcrypt is the first thing to fall over when Nano runs dry.

Separately, your last two deploys of `e8130157` failed to boot (build passed, process exits 1) — production is safe on `74bc8646`, but your next push will fail until that's fixed. Want me to dig into that one now?
